Albert Hanlin Crews Jr., born on March 23, 1929, in El Dorado, Arkansas, was an American Air Force officer, pilot, and astronaut selectee. He earned a Bachelor of Science in chemical engineering from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in 1950 and a Master of Science in aeronautical engineering from the U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology in 1959. He also completed pilot training and became a qualified test pilot through the Aerospace Research Pilot School.
Crews was selected in 1965 as a military astronaut for the United States Air Force's Manned Orbiting Laboratory (MOL) program, which was intended as a reconnaissance platform in space. Albert Hanlin Crews Jr., born on March 23, 1929, in El Dorado, Arkansas, was an American Air Force officer, pilot, and astronaut selectee. He earned a Bachelor of Science in chemical engineering from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in 1950 and a Master of Science in aeronautical engineering from the U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology in 1959. He also completed pilot training and became a qualified test pilot through the Aerospace Research Pilot School.
Crews was selected in 1965 as a military astronaut for the United States Air Force's Manned Orbiting Laboratory (MOL) program, which was intended as a reconnaissance platform in space. Albert Hanlin Crews Jr., born on March 23, 1929, in El Dorado, Arkansas, was an American Air Force officer, pilot, and astronaut selectee. He earned a Bachelor of Science in chemical engineering from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in 1950 and a Master of Science in aeronautical engineering from the U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology in 1959. He also completed pilot training and became a qualified test pilot through the Aerospace Research Pilot School.
Crews was selected in 1965 as a military astronaut for the United States Air Force's Manned Orbiting Laboratory (MOL) program, which was intended as a reconnaissance platform in space.
